data.title: An AI acceleration initiative over six months, [the whole company activated by AKO in February.]
data.sub: This is every company's first AI transformation.
data.left:
**AI policy and risk.** Standardizing and unifying the company's AI policy ahead of mass adoption, avoiding costly economic, legal, and reputational risks.
**Capability.** Make every role and level AI-first.
**Resistance.** Change threatens identity. Will what people were good at still matter, and will the new job be as interesting?
**L&D capacity.** Your strongest AI people have day jobs, and aren't always the strongest teachers.
**Tracking impact.** Challenging to report ROI, progress, and impact to the board.
data.right:
**Output that scales without headcount.** ICs become managers of agents, scaling their impact.
**An AI-first operating model.** Every role, process, and project is redesigned to be AI-first.
**Company engagement.** A workforce that is excited about being AI-first, and feels prepared for the future rather than scared.
**Customer alignment.** SheerID supports many of the most advanced AI companies. Keeping up with AI fluency keeps you aligned with them.
**Clear ROI.** Board-ready reporting on the transformation and its impact.

data.title: An 18-month roadmap: [October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2028.]
data.months: Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan, Feb · AKO
data.rows:
Foundations | Everyone, self-paced | 0-2 solid All ~185 employees
AI Builder Program | SLT / ELT | 1-3 solid 20 leaders
AI Builder Program | Phase 2 squads | 2-4 light In roadmap order
ELT / SLT workshops | Three, half-day | 2-3.2 light Three workshops
Cluster support | Domain experts, 1:1s | 1-5 light Six clusters, twelve experts paired
AI Innovation Sprint | Hackathon | 3.3-4.7 solid Squads ship agents
AI engineers | Build support | 0-5 dashed 10 hours a month, on demand, for AI engineering or AI leadership support
data.note: **Why October.** A November start runs into the holidays, which slow progress and momentum. Driving baseline fluency in October, ahead of the phased enablement waves, has produced the strongest adoption while mitigating near-term compliance, security, and reputational risks.

data.title: The roadmap continues: [February 2027 onward.]
data.months: Feb · AKO, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul
data.rows:

ROI and behavior change | Workshop, March | 1-2 solid Metrics, feedback loops, and what to do next
Redesign squads | Workflows and roles | 0-6 light Rolling all year, in ROI order
On-demand support | 1:1s and AI engineers | 0-6 dashed Monthly 1:1s continue, remaining bank hours drawn on demand
data.cols:
Continued access | Employees retain access to the AI Builder Program and its updated curriculum through March 2028, so skills compound as models change.
On-demand support | The AIA, squad leaders, and executives keep 1:1 support from domain experts, with AI engineers on call for technical help.
ROI analysis | Metrics, reporting, and feedback loops to track ROI and flag opportunities for cost savings, process improvement, and continued enablement.

data.title: Near-term productivity, [while mitigating risks.]
data.c1:
**See the potential.** Where AI actually fits their own job, and what it can do beyond search.
**Use it effectively.** Giving AI real context, staying organized, and getting output worth keeping.
**Use it responsibly.** Security, honesty about what AI produces, and control of what it costs.
data.h2: Four live sessions over two weeks
data.c2:
Deliver a working product, end to end
Automate communication in your voice, analyze data, and create presentations with AI
Design role-specific skills
Demo day and certificates. Access included for the SLT / ELT and every wave that follows
data.c3:
**AI policy reinforcement.** Your AI policy and data classification, taught in the same round, so level set and policy launch are one motion.
**Data-privacy guardrails.** A five-person design group goes first, so data boundaries are set before the company-wide launch.
**Board-ready reporting.** Baseline and post competency, completion, compliance, and adoption, reported to the AI Acceleration team each cohort.

data.title: How progress [gets measured.]
data.c1: Before the program, participants are surveyed to baseline current AI competency. After, a follow-up survey gauges the lift, person by person.
data.c2: Attendance, recording views, and completion tracked throughout and reported to the AI Acceleration team, so you can see who is progressing and who needs support.
data.c3: Agents and automations built inside the program, counted per cohort, then function-specific builds from the Sprint, showcased at AKO.
data.note: These become the first numbers behind the ROI gates in your own plan, and the progress report your board is expecting.
